notes: Class: the same as OWNER-CAPTURE-NIL0-INTERN. books/owner-reclaim-seal.lisp fn-orcs-predict-rows interns every wire record of the rewritten history at the single KEYRING and GENERATION it is handed (fn-orcs-held-of), and fn-rcw-rebuild-of-the-chunked-capture-is-the-full-open / fn-orcp-rebuild-is-the-full-open take those predicted rows as the history the full open (fn-ock-recover-full) replays. A restart replays the rewritten history through fn-ssr-intern-step, which freezes the keyring and generation in force before each row (books/store-checkpoint-fold.lisp). After a keyring rotation the two differ for the articles before the rotation or after it.

Evidence: tests/acl2/store-checkpoint-fold-tests.lisp, the assert-event on fn-orcs-predict-rows: on the log enroll, article A, rotate, article B no single (keyring, generation) pair gives the replay's rows (not at nil/0, not at the rotated keyring/2).

Fix shape: fn-orcs-predict-rows over the rewritten wire rows becomes fn-scka-fold-at from the seed of the base identity (fn-scka-intern-at), carried per chunk like fn-rcw-canon-acc-step; fn-rcw-predict-acc-step carries the identity in the accumulator already (fn-sco-at 3 acc); the seal quantum must intern the same rows. Needs the Ruling 22 package (ownership-reclamation).
Not verified here: whether the live swap passes the store's current keyring/generation or nil/0 (host/owner-host.lisp near 5619); either way the rows are single-context.
